title: Things to Do in Saputara: Lake, Sunset Point, Waterfalls & Tribal Culture
seoTitle: Things to Do in Saputara: Lake, Views & Falls | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Saputara: boating on Saputara Lake, sunrise and sunset points, the ropeway to Table Point, Gira Falls, the Artist Village and Warli art, the tribal museum, gardens, the monsoon festival, Vansda National Park and Hatgadh Fort.
dek: Gujarat's only hill station, on a plateau in the Sahyadri range of the Dang forests, known for its lake, viewpoints and monsoon waterfalls.
searchIntent: Families and weekenders from Gujarat and Maharashtra planning one or two days in Saputara.
intro: Saputara, at about 1,000 metres in the Dang district of south-eastern Gujarat, sits on a plateau of the Sahyadri (Western Ghats) close to the Maharashtra border. The name means abode of serpents, and snake worship is part of local tribal tradition. The Dangs are home to Bhil, Kunbi and Warli communities.

The things to do in Saputara are relaxed: boating on the lake, watching sunrise and sunset from the viewpoints, riding the ropeway, visiting gardens and the Artist Village, and driving down to Gira Falls. It is at its best in the monsoon, when the hills are green, waterfalls pour off every cliff and the town holds its monsoon festival.
One or two days is enough. July to February is the best time, especially the monsoon and early winter.

items.name: Go boating on Saputara Lake
body: Saputara Lake, at the centre of the town, has rowing and pedal boats, and a promenade lined with food stalls. It is busiest in the evening.
Around the lake, stalls sell corn, bhajias and local snacks, and horse and camel rides are offered on the shore. In the monsoon, clouds often drift down to the water's edge.

items.name: Walk through the gardens
body: The Rose Garden, Step Garden and Lake Garden are well kept and pleasant for a stroll, especially after the monsoon.

items.name: Visit the tribal museum
body: The museum in town has displays on the dress, tools, musical instruments and way of life of the Dang tribal communities.

items.name: Watch sunrise from Valley View Point
body: Valley View Point, also used as the sunrise point, looks east over the Dang forests and valleys.

items.name: Watch sunset from Sunset Point
body: Sunset Point, a short walk or ride from town, faces west over the Sahyadri ridges and is the town's most popular evening spot.
Paragliding flights have been offered from the hills during the monsoon festival and in season; check with licensed operators.

items.name: Ride the ropeway to Table Point
body: A ropeway links the Sunset Point area with Table Point (Governor's Hill), a flat hilltop with pony rides and views over the valley.

items.name: See Gira Falls
body: Gira Falls, near Waghai about 50 km away, is a wide waterfall on the Ambika river that is spectacular in the monsoon. A viewing area lets visitors see it from close by.
The falls are about 30 metres wide in full flow, and the area around them has stalls selling bamboo crafts made by local artisans. Swimming at the base is not allowed.

items.name: Visit the Artist Village
body: The Artist Village, a short drive from town, promotes local tribal art such as Warli painting, with workshops, a gallery and simple stays.
Warli art uses simple white figures on mud-coloured walls to show village life, harvests and festivals. Visitors can join short workshops and buy paintings directly from artists.

items.name: Walk in Vansda National Park
body: Vansda National Park, about 50 km away, protects moist deciduous forest with leopards, giant squirrels, deer and many birds.
The park lies along the Ambika river, and its dense teak and bamboo forests are good for birdwatching. Forest department guides can arrange walks and jeep drives.

items.name: See Hatgadh Fort
body: Hatgadh Fort, just across the border in Maharashtra, is a Maratha fort reached by a short trek, with views over the plateau.

items.name: Attend the monsoon festival
body: The Saputara Monsoon Festival, held in August, brings cultural performances, adventure activities and events to the plateau. The Dang Darbar, a tribal fair at Ahwa around Holi, is another major event.

facts.Best time: August; Holi for the Dang Darbar

items.name: July to September
body: The monsoon festival, waterfalls and misty green hills; the most popular season.

items.name: October to February
body: Clear, cool days and pleasant nights.

items.name: March to June
body: Warm, but cooler than the plains of Gujarat.

byTraveller.text: Lake boating, the ropeway, gardens and Gira Falls.
Sunset Point, monsoon mist and quiet walks.
The Artist Village, the tribal museum and the Dang Darbar.
Drive up on Saturday for the lake and Sunset Point, see Gira Falls on Sunday and return in the afternoon.

oneDay: Go boating on the lake in the morning and visit the tribal museum and gardens. After lunch, drive to Gira Falls, and return for the ropeway to Table Point and sunset at Sunset Point.
tips: The nearest railway station is Waghai (narrow gauge) or Nashik Road; Surat has the nearest airport, about four hours away.
Gujarat's dry laws apply in Saputara.
Roads can be slippery in the monsoon.
Weekends in the monsoon are crowded; book ahead.
Carry a light raincoat in the monsoon and a jacket in winter; the plateau is cooler than the plains.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Saputara?
faqs.a: Go boating on the lake, watch sunrise and sunset from the viewpoints, ride the ropeway, see Gira Falls, visit the Artist Village and the tribal museum, and attend the monsoon festival.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Saputara?
faqs.a: July to February, especially the monsoon for waterfalls and greenery.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Saputara?
How far is Saputara from Nashik?
faqs.a: About 80 km, roughly two hours by road.

faqs.q: Is Saputara good for a family trip?
faqs.a: Yes. The lake, ropeway, gardens, museum and nearby waterfalls are easy outings, and the town is small and safe.

faqs.q: How far is Gira Falls from Saputara?
faqs.a: About 50 km, roughly an hour and a half by road, near Waghai.
